title: Tree TPS is overhead-bound, not verify-kernel-bound: profile + attack the committer/drafter overhead (the '3% tax' was verify-only)
finding: TPS = committed_per_step / wall_per_step. At B=1 the realized rate is overhead-dominated. Worked example (cat6 vs native E5, B=1 t0.6): cat6 commits +15.7% tokens/step (4.76 vs 4.11) but its step is ~+11% LONGER -> net only ~+4% deploy-TPS. The accept gain is ~70% eaten by the slower step.
key_correction: The previously-quoted '~3% kernel tax' is ONLY the VERIFY FORWARD (s/fwd_gpu = our forked-FA2 attn + GDN-tree-scan). That is real + directly measured (cat6 verify 0.137 == native 0.137 ~0%; cat9 +5%; ~3% banked at B=1). BUT it UNDERSTATED the tree's total step-cost-over-native: the bigger cost is in the OVERHEAD bucket (drafter/propose + committer + scheduler/gaps), which the timer does NOT bracket. Derived overhead: native ~0.082 (wall-span basis) / 0.094 (deploy-TPS basis); cat6 ~0.12 => +~0.026s/step (~+30% overhead). THAT is where the accept gain leaks, and a chunk of it is OUR code (the device multidraft committer especially).

OURS: tree-construction / propose_tree topology+wiring (the KIND -> tree shape) - ours
OURS_partial: verify forward: attn (forked FA2 FR13_FA2_TREE_BIAS) + GDN-tree-scan are ours; in_proj/MLP/GEMM/lm-head are stock
STOCK_vLLM_not_ours: scheduler / engine loop / inter-step gaps (fixed per step)
base MTP head weights + base proposer forward
ownership_of_overhead.implication: A real chunk of the overhead (committer + tree-propose) is OURS -> attackable. The fixed scheduler/gap part is stock -> not. So the open question is how much of the +0.026s is ours (optimizable) vs stock (only accept-amortizable).

caveats_on_the_number: The +0.026s overhead is (1) DERIVED (wall = committed/deploy-TPS), not directly measured; (2) basis-dependent (wall-span vs deploy-TPS give native 0.082 vs 0.094); (3) MID-ARM (cat6 2/4 when computed) so it will move; (4) LUMPED - cannot split committer vs drafter vs fixed-gap from current instrumentation (timer brackets verify forward only).
future_work: PROFILE the 4-way per-step split (drafter/propose | verify-forward | committer | fixed scheduler-gap) via CUDA events around propose() + the committer (or an nsys/torch-profiler boot). Dedicated run; the current run only times the verify forward.
Recompute the overhead at FINAL-arm consistent counters (not mid-arm derived) for native vs each tree shape; report the clean committed/wall decomposition per arm.

Quantify how much of the tree overhead is OURS (committer + tree-propose, attackable) vs STOCK (scheduler/gap, only accept-amortizable). If mostly ours -> big optimization opportunity (cheaper committer); if mostly stock -> the lever stays accept.

Complementary lever = SUFFIX DECODING: TPS = committed/wall, so a cheap-step low-accept shape (suffix automaton: tiny drafting+commit cost) can match TPS even with bad accept. The goal shape = high committed AND cheap step. Revisit suffix-decoding (early git history) as the cheap-overhead route.
